advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile whether `~/.rebar-serena-mirror` is a `git worktree` (docs) or a `read-only origin/main mirror` (.mcp.json comment) and state one mechanism consistently.
evidence: docs/mcp-client-setup.md:125: `origin/main` mirror at `~/.rebar-serena-mirror` (a `git worktree` of this repository) that
.mcp.json:12-13: "(upgrade with `uv tool upgrade serena-agent`), and provision the read-only", "origin/main mirror at ~/.rebar-serena-mirror (see AGENTS.md)."
advisory.finding: The mirror prerequisite is described inconsistently: docs call `~/.rebar-serena-mirror` 'a `git worktree` of this repository' while the `.mcp.json` comment calls it a 'read-only origin/main mirror' — a git worktree and a mirror clone are different mechanisms, which can misdirect an operator provisioning the prerequisite.
scenarios: An operator follows the docs and creates a worktree, or follows the comment and creates a mirror clone, and gets divergent Serena indexing behavior.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the `~/.rebar-serena-mirror` provisioning cross-reference in `.mcp.json` point to a source that actually documents how to create the mirror (or add that provisioning step to the cited owner).
evidence: .mcp.json:13: "origin/main mirror at ~/.rebar-serena-mirror (see AGENTS.md)." — the changed comment names AGENTS.md as the owner of the mirror-provisioning prerequisite

AGENTS.md:423-425 describes the Serena mirror only conceptually ("Serena reads a dedicated read-only mirror of origin/main ... and that mirror refreshes on a poll interval") and never names `~/.rebar-serena-mirror` nor gives any command to provision/create it
search for `.rebar-serena-mirror` across the repo returns hits only in `.mcp.json` and `docs/mcp-client-setup.md`, confirming AGENTS.md carries no such provisioning instructions
advisory.finding: `.mcp.json:13` directs the reader to `AGENTS.md` to learn how to provision the `~/.rebar-serena-mirror` mirror that the new serena entry requires, but the AGENTS.md section it points at never mentions that path or how to create it, so the cited owner lacks the provisioning content the reader needs.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the serena-agent install to a specific tag/commit (e.g. `git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@<tag-or-sha>`) for reproducible, verifiable installs.
evidence: docs/mcp-client-setup.md: `uv tool install --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena serena-agent   # once per machine`
No `@<tag|commit>` ref appended to the git URL in either .mcp.json comment or docs
advisory.finding: The serena-agent dependency is installed from an unpinned git source (`git+https://github.com/oraios/serena` with no @ref/tag/commit), so `uv tool install`/`uv tool upgrade` resolve whatever upstream HEAD is current at run time, giving no reproducible or pinned version.
scenarios: Two developers install on different days and get different serena versions
Upstream introduces a breaking or malicious change that flows in via `uv tool upgrade`
advisory.suggested_fix: Append a pinned ref to the git URL in both .mcp.json and docs, e.g. `uv tool install --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@v<X.Y.Z> serena-agent`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/enforce a provenance check (pinned commit + verified checksum or signature) for the serena-agent install.
evidence: docs describe `uv tool install --from git+...` as the sole install step with no hash/signature check
No lockfile or manifest entry accompanies this new external dependency in the diff
ABSENCE: nothing records or verifies the installed serena-agent version/provenance
advisory.finding: No integrity/provenance verification (hash, signature, or lockfile) is documented or committed for the externally-installed serena-agent binary that the project now depends on.
scenarios: A compromised upstream or MITM during install ships a modified binary that runs unverified

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm `copilot mcp get rebar` / `claude mcp list` still exit 0 with the new `type: local` serena entry present but its `${HOME}/...bin/serena` command absent under the scratch HOME.
evidence: _mask_home plants an empty scratch HOME (test line 326-328), so the serena command path resolves to a nonexistent file under that HOME.
dropped.finding: The existing client-binary acceptance tests copy the whole `.mcp.json` (now including the `type: local` serena entry whose command is `${HOME}/.local/share/uv/tools/serena-agent/bin/serena`) into a scratch HOME where that binary does not exist; if `copilot mcp get`/`claude mcp list` validate local server command paths, `proc.returncode == 0` could fail, silently coupling the rebar acceptance canary to an unrelated, unprovisioned serena binary.
scenarios: Running with RUN_CLIENT_BINARY_TESTS enabled on a host where the CLI eagerly validates local server command paths.
